questions.q: Sort each mistake by the kind of error it is.
items: A missing colon at the end of an if line
A loop that runs one time too many
questions.feedback: A syntax error stops the program running at all. A logic error lets it run and gives the wrong answer.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.1 Lesson 10 — Fault finder, station 3: Telling them apart

questions.q: Explain the difference between a syntax error and a logic error.

markPoints.concept: a syntax error breaks the rules of the language
markPoints.exemplar: A syntax error breaks the rules of the language.

markPoints.concept: so the program will not run at all
accept: will not run|cannot run|does not run|refuses to run|stops|fails to run|crash|will not compile|error message
markPoints.exemplar: This means the program will not run at all.

markPoints.concept: a logic error lets the program run but produces the wrong result
markPoints.exemplar: A logic error lets the program run but gives the wrong result.

questions.example: A syntax error breaks the rules of the language, such as a missing bracket, so the program will not run at all. A logic error does not break any rule, so the program runs perfectly happily, but the instructions do not do what the programmer intended and the output is wrong.
questions.paraphrase: A syntax error is a breach of the language's grammar and stops the code executing. A logic error obeys the grammar, so the code runs, but it gives an answer that is not the one wanted.
questions.feedback: Three ideas: what a syntax error is, what it does, and what a logic error does instead.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.1 Lesson 10 — Fault finder, station 3: Telling them apart

questions.q: This program is meant to print the average of the three numbers. What does it actually print?
questions.code:
a = 4
b = 6
c = 8
print(a + b + c / 3)
questions.feedback: Division happens before addition, so only c is divided by 3: 4 + 6 + 2.666... The brackets are missing. This is a logic error, not a syntax error — the program runs quite happily.
questions.hint: Which operation does Python do first?
questions.misconception: Expecting 6 assumes the brackets are there.
